title: R’ Chanina or Chananyah, son of R’ Yose the Galilean

paragraphs: R’ Chanina (or Chananyah), son of R’ Yose the Galilean. (Tanna).

Hyman describes him as the leading sage of his generation in Usha’s Sanhedrin under the presidency of R’ Shimon ben Gamliel. Rosh Hashanah 32a [31b in Hyman] relates that when the court sanctified the year at Usha, R’ Yochanan ben Beroka went down before R’ Shimon ben Gamliel. On the second day, R’ Chanina, son of R’ Yose the Galilean, went down and acted according to R’ Akiva, etc. Nedarim, chapter 6, halakhah 8, Sanhedrin, chapter 1, halakhah 2, and Sifra, Emor at Hyman’s section 178, have R’ Chananyah son of R’ Yose the Galilean. He is also mentioned in Chullin 12a, disputing with R’ Yehudah about one whose kids and chickens were lost and who went and found them slaughtered.
The statement is also brought in Bava Metzia 24b and Tosefta Chullin, chapter 2, where Hyman gives the reading Chanina.

notes.text: The checked Usha account is on Rosh Hashanah 32a, while Hyman supplies 31b. The second-day phrase is retained; the Gemara itself discusses its interpretation. Sifra’s קע״ח is 178, not 78.

No new primary scalar was returned. RoshHashanah 32a is an inherited recorded match alongside Hyman’s 31b, not a fresh whole text inspection. The second-day phrase and sanctified-the-YEAR wording are kept without importing a festival-calendar solution. גדול הדור means the leading sage of his generation, not merely an unspecified leading sage; the status and Usha presidency are Hyman’s characterizations. All personal titles in this supplied notice are abbreviated and remain R-prime, including ShimonbenGamliel’s contextually expanded name; no full Rabban title is supplied here. Chanina/Chananyah and the unprefixed final Chanina remain distinct source forms, not automatically harmonized. Sifra קע״ח is 178 not 78. The lost kids/chickens were subsequently found SLAUGHTERED by their owner, and the source explicitly says he WENT and found them. All source holds remain.

The Usha account is in the consulted Rosh Hashanah 32a. In its continuation Rav Chisda explains the second day as the following year. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 6:8 and Sanhedrin 1:2 give Yishmael son of Yochanan ben Beroka for the first prayer and Chananyah son of Yose the Galilean for the second. Sifra, Emor, section 11:5, and the scan at Daat, p. ר״ג, give Shimon son of Yochanan ben Beroka first and Chananyah second. Hyman cites Sifra section 178. The consulted Chullin 12a has Chanina permitting the slaughtered animals. Bava Metzia 24b calls the finder Chanina and names Chananyah son of Yose the Galilean in the cited ruling. The consulted Tosefta Chullin, chapter 2, gives a theft case in which Chananyah disqualifies and Yehudah permits. In the continuation, Rabbi finds Chananyah’s view persuasive for a find in the house and Yehudah’s for a find in refuse.
